question: After which Prime Minister was a sports award named in India? (RRB JE CBT I (31/05/2019) Shift 1)
options: P.V. Narasimha Rao
V.P. Singh
Charan Singh
Rajiv Gandhi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Rajiv Gandhi

Explanation:
In India, the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award (now renamed as Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award) was named after former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi. This award was instituted in 1991-92 to recognize outstanding performance by sportspersons. However, in 2021, it was renamed in honor of hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand. Rajiv Gandhi served as the Prime Minister of India from 1984 to 1989 and was the youngest person to hold the office. The award includes a medal, a certificate, and a cash prize. It is considered one of the highest honors in Indian sports. The award is conferred by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

question: Article 17 of Indian Constitution deals with - (RRB JE CBT I (01/06/2019) Shift 2)
options: Right to education
Abolition of untouchability
Abolition of titles
Equality before law
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Abolition of untouchability

Explanation:
Article 17 of the Indian Constitution deals with the abolition of untouchability. It is a fundamental right that abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form. Discrimination based on untouchability is considered a constitutional offense. This provision is crucial for ensuring social equality and human dignity. Under this article, the state can enact laws to punish any disability arising from untouchability. It provides protection to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

question: Which of the following departments comes under the Ministry of Finance in India? (RRB JE CBT I (01/06/2019) Shift 2)
options: Department of Economic Affairs
All of the options
Department of Revenue
Department of Expenditure
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is All of the options

Explanation:
The Ministry of Finance in India oversees several key departments responsible for the country's economic policies and financial management. The Department of Economic Affairs handles economic policy, budgeting, and capital markets. The Department of Revenue is responsible for the collection of direct and indirect taxes. The Department of Expenditure manages government spending and financing of schemes. Additionally, the Department of Financial Services regulates banking, insurance, and financial institutions, and the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management manages public sector investments. Thus, all the given options fall under the Ministry of Finance.

question: When was the internal emergency declared in India during the period of Indira Gandhi as Prime Minister? (RRB JE CBT I (01/06/2019) Shift 2)
options: 1984
1973
1978
1975
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1975

Explanation:
The internal emergency was declared in India on June 25, 1975 during the tenure of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. It was imposed under Article 352 of the Constitution on grounds of internal disturbance. The emergency lasted for 21 months, ending on March 21, 1977. During this period, civil liberties were suspended, press censorship was imposed, and opposition leaders were arrested. This emergency is considered a controversial chapter in Indian political history.

question: Which of the following High Courts has the largest jurisdiction in the country? (RRB JE CBT I (01/06/2019) Shift 3)
options: Allahabad High Court
Gauhati High Court
Bombay High Court
Calcutta High Court
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Gauhati High Court

Explanation:
The Gauhati High Court has the largest jurisdiction among the given options. It covers the states of Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, and Arunachal Pradesh. Established in 1948, its principal seat is in Guwahati, with permanent benches in Nagaland, Mizoram, and Arunachal Pradesh. In comparison, the Allahabad High Court covers only Uttar Pradesh, the Bombay High Court covers Maharashtra, Goa, and the union territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, and the Calcutta High Court covers West Bengal and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The Gauhati High Court's jurisdiction is the most extensive in terms of geographical area and number of states. This makes it the correct answer.

☛ When was Gauhati High Court established? → 1948

question: Which of the following statements is FALSE? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 1)

According to Article 74, the President will act only on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
All members of the Council of Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President.
Article 76 provides for a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 76 provides for a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

Explanation:
This statement is false because Article 76 deals with the Attorney General of India, not the Council of Ministers. The Council of Ministers is provided under Article 74 and Article 75. Article 74 states that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President. Article 75 deals with the appointment, tenure, and responsibility of ministers. According to Article 77, all executive actions of the Government of India shall be taken in the name of the President. All members of the Council of Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President.

question: Which Amendment has made the Right to Education a Fundamental Right? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 1)

question: Who is the head of Union Executive in India? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: The Governor
Chief Justice of Supreme Court
The Prime Minister
The President
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The President

Explanation:
According to Article 53 of the Indian Constitution, the executive power of the Union is vested in the President. The President is the constitutional head of the Union Executive. He is the first citizen and the symbol of the nation. The President is elected by an electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the Legislative Assemblies of states. Although the President is the head of the executive, he acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers (Article 74). The Prime Minister is the real executive head, while the President is the formal head. The Governor is the head of the state executive, and the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court is the head of the judiciary.

question_hi: भारत में केंद्रीय कार्यपालिका का प्रमुख कौन है? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 1)

प्रधानमंत्री
राष्ट्रपति
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है राष्ट्रपति

Explanation:
भारत के संविधान के अनुच्छेद 53 के अनुसार, केंद्रीय कार्यपालिका की शक्तियाँ राष्ट्रपति में निहित हैं। राष्ट्रपति केंद्रीय कार्यपालिका का संवैधानिक प्रमुख होता है। वह भारत का प्रथम नागरिक और राष्ट्र का प्रतीक है। राष्ट्रपति का चुनाव निर्वाचक मंडल द्वारा किया जाता है जिसमें संसद के दोनों सदनों और राज्यों की विधानसभाओं के निर्वाचित सदस्य शामिल होते हैं। यद्यपि राष्ट्रपति कार्यपालिका का प्रमुख है, वह मंत्रिपरिषद की सलाह से बंधा होता है (अनुच्छेद 74)। प्रधानमंत्री वास्तविक कार्यकारी प्रमुख है, जबकि राष्ट्रपति औपचारिक प्रमुख है। राज्यपाल राज्य स्तर पर कार्यपालिका का प्रमुख होता है, और सर्वोच्च न्यायालय का मुख्य न्यायाधीश न्यायपालिका का प्रमुख है।

question: Which of the following is responsible for the protection and enforcement of Fundamental Rights in India? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: Supreme Court of India
Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)
Election Commission of India
National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Supreme Court of India

Explanation:
The Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution. Under Article 32, citizens can directly approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of these rights. The Supreme Court has the power to issue writs like Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto. It acts as the guardian and protector of Fundamental Rights. Other options: UPSC selects for civil services, Election Commission conducts elections, and NHRC monitors human rights, but the enforcement of Fundamental Rights primarily lies with the Supreme Court. The Court ensures that no law or executive action violates these rights, making it the ultimate authority for their protection.

question: The ____________ has appellate jurisdiction on all subordinate courts in the district.  (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 2)
